newsitem.title: USA: Zurich Kemper funds top high-yld outflows in week.
newsitem.headline: Zurich Kemper funds top high-yld outflows in week.

text.p: Zurich Kemper Investment's High-Yield A and High-Yield B funds had net redemptions of $255 million in the latest week, representing more than one-third of total cash outflows from like funds, according to AMG Data Services.

Other large net redemptions were recorded from: Fidelity Advisors high-yield fund at $50 million; Strong Capital Management's high-yield fund at $42 million; PIMCO Advisors LP's high-yield fund at $33 million; and Federated Investors Inc's high-yield fund at $30 million.
Calls to a fund manager and corporate communications of Zurich Kemper Investments were not returned.

Cash outflows from high-yield bond funds excluding distributions totaled $662.8 million in the week ended April 2, AMG said. They bring the total outflows to more than $1.4 billion since the reports turned negative three weeks ago.
They are the largest consecutive net redemptions since the Federal Reserve began its series of short-term interest rate hikes in early 1994, said AMG President Robert Adler.
Net asset value performance of high-yield bond funds since early March is negative 3.38 percent, he said. However, he said it was too soon to say if the trend will persist.

"The question is whether or not the negative market will continue to rattle investors or, if the market stabilizes somewhat, history has shown investors come back into these funds with a vengeance," Adler said.

One high-yield fund manager in New York who declined to be named said he saw redemptions peaking at the latest levels. But negative flows may continue for a few weeks before they begin to "bounce around stable," he said.
